verdict.rationale: Semgrep documents writing custom rules to control what it detects. It also offers an `entropy` metavariable analyzer, which suits high-randomness token detection, and generic pattern matching for unsupported file types. Rules can be tested, published privately to an organization, and run in pre-commit to stop secrets reaching Git history. However, no evidence shows custom rules plugging into Semgrep Secrets specifically, such as custom secret rules with validators that test internal token formats. missing for 10: explicit docs on custom Semgrep Secrets rules for proprietary token formats, custom validation of internal secrets, independent or hands-on corroboration of custom secret-rule authoring.

support.subject: As a security-engineer, I can define custom detection rules for my organization's internal token and secret formats

citations.quote: you can write custom rules to determine what Semgrep detects in your repositories
Currently, this syntax supports two analyzers: `redos` and `entropy`.
Users with Semgrep Code's Team or Enterprise tier can publish rules to the Semgrep Registry as private rules that are not visible to those outside their organization.
Semgrep provides a testing mechanism for your rules.
This is helpful in preventing secrets and security issues from leaking into your Git history.
